title: Windows Solitaire was written by an intern, for himself.
description:
Windows Solitaire was written by an intern, for himself. Wes Cherry made it in his own time in summer 1988, for Windows 2.1.

He had been playing a Mac version instead of studying. Cherry says he wanted a Windows version for himself.

Designed the card deck. Solitaire shipped in Windows 3.0, released 22 May 1990.

He received no royalties. Cherry says he was supplied with an IBM XT to fix bugs and was perfectly fine with that.

Monthly players across 200 markets at the 30th anniversary in 2020, according to Engadget.

A student's side project became one of the most played games ever.

Sources:
- https://finance.yahoo.com/news/guy-wrote-windows-solitaire-did-231250280.html - Yahoo Finance quoting Wes Cherry; established that he wrote it in his own time as an intern in summer 1988 for Windows 2.1, that he was not paid royalties beyond being supplied an IBM XT to fix bugs, and that he wanted a Windows version of a Mac solitaire game he had played instead of studying.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Solitaire - Wikipedia; established inclusion in Windows 3.0 (released 22 May 1990), Susan Kare designing the card deck, the reported aim of easing users into the graphical interface, and the 2019 World Video Game Hall of Fame entry.
- https://www.engadget.com/microsoft-solitaire-turns-30-today-bouncy-bouncy-094904319.html - Engadget; established the figure of 35 million players per month across 200 markets and 65 languages at the 30th anniversary.
